events.title: Indian Shares Seen Little Changed As US Midterm Election Results Trickle In
events.description: Indian shares are seen opening flat to lower on Wednesday after a strong four-session rally. That said, a weakening dollar in overseas markets, falling U.S. Treasury yields and steadier oil prices may help limit losses, if any.

events.title: Higher Open Called For Thai Stock Market
events.description: The Thai stock market has finished lower in six straight sessions, sliding more than 85 points or 5.5 percent in that span. The Stock Exchange of Thailand now sits just above the 1,490-point plateau although it may halt its slide on Wednesday.

events.title: China Services PMI Ebbs In October - Caixin
events.description: The services sector in China continued to expand in October, albeit at a slower pace, the latest survey from S&P Global revealed on Wednesday with a business PMI score of 50.8.

events.title: Renewed Support Likely For Indonesia Stock Market
events.description: The Indonesia stock market turned emphatically lower again on Tuesday, one day after ending the two-day losing streak in which it had dropped more than 225 points or 4 percent. The Jakarta Composite Index now sits just above the 4,900-point plateau although it's likely to rebound on Wednesday.

events.title: Japanese Market Sharply Lower
events.description: The Japanese stock market is trading sharply lower on Wednesday, extending the losses in the previous session, following the mixed cues from Wall Street overnight. The Nikkei 225 is falling well below the 61,850 level, with weakness in financial and technology stocks partially offset by gains in exporter stocks.

events.title: Hong Kong Stock Market May Spin Its Wheels On Wednesday
events.description: The Hong Kong stock market has moved higher in three straight sessions, collecting more than 560 points or 2.5 percent along the way. The Hang Seng now sits just above the 23,525-point plateau although it may run out of steam on Wednesday.

events.title: Australian Market Modestly Lower
events.description: Australian shares are trading modestly lower on Wednesday, reversing the gains in the previous session, with the benchmark S&P/ASX 200 falling to near the 8,850 level, following the mixed cues from Wall Street overnight, with weakness in mining and financial stocks partially offset by gains in energy and technology stocks.

events.title: Rebound Predicted For China Stock Market
events.description: The China stock market turned lower again on Tuesday, one day after ending the two-day losing streak in which it had dropped more than 80 points or 2.2 percent. The Shanghai Composite Index now sits just beneath the 3,610-point plateau although it may find renewed support on Wednesday.

events.title: Japan Monetary Base Sinks 13.6% On Year In October
events.description: The monetary base in Japan was down 13.6 percent on year in October, the Bank of Japan said on Wednesday - coming in at 532.571 trillion yen.

events.title: Singapore Private Sector PMI Slows In October - S&P Global
events.description: The private sector in Singapore continued to expand in October, albeit at a slower pace, the latest survey from S&P Global revealed on Wednesday with a business PMI score of 56.7.

events.title: Hong Kong Private Sector Expands In October - S&P Global
events.description: The private sector in Hong Kong moved back into expansion territory in October, the latest survey from S&P Global revealed on Wednesday with a business PMI score of 50.2.

events.title: Bargain Hunting May Boost Taiwan Stock Market
events.description: The Taiwan stock market has finished lower in four straight sessions, tumbling more than 3,700 points or 8.2 percent along the way. The Taiwan Stock Exchange now sits just above the 43,300-point plateau although it's overdue for support on Wednesday.

events.title: Singapore Stock Market May Halt Losing Streak
events.description: The Singapore stock market has moved lower in four straight sessions, slumping almost 130 points or 2.5 percent along the way. The Straits Times Index now sits just beneath the 5,270-point plateau although it may stop the bleeding on Wednesday.
